properties.name: Crude Oil (Niger Delta)
properties.summary: Nigeria's dominant mineral resource — Africa's largest crude producer, concentrated in the Niger Delta.
properties.description: Nigeria is Africa's largest crude-oil producer and a leading OPEC member. Reserves are concentrated in the Niger Delta basin, offshore deepwater, and shallows of the Gulf of Guinea. The Bonny Light and Forcados 40° blends are internationally traded benchmarks, and most crude is exported from Bonny, Forcados, Escravos, and Qua Iboe terminals. The industry has driven federal revenue since the 1970s while creating extensive environmental remediation, security, and political-economy challenges in the delta.

properties.name: Natural Gas (LNG & Associated)
properties.summary: Africa's largest proven gas reserves; LNG exports via Bonny NLNG and growing domestic gas & NIPCo networks.
properties.description: Nigeria holds Africa's largest proven natural-gas reserves, historically seen as associated gas flared from oil production. The Nigeria LNG (NLNG) plant at Bonny now ranks among the world's top LNG exporters, while the Escravos Gas-to-Liquids (EGTL), Obiafu-Obrikom gas gathering, Oben-Geregu pipeline, and the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) pipeline build a domestic gas grid for power, industry, and petrochemicals.
properties.reserveNote: ~200+ trillion standard cubic feet proven (Tcf) — largest in Africa
properties.productionNote: NLNG ~22 Mtpa (6 trains); domestic gas expanding via AKK pipeline & DS Phases
properties.type: Associated & non-associated gas; LNG, LPG, CNG, GTL products
properties.economy: LNG exports, domestic power/gas-to-plant, fertiliser, new petrochemical hubs.
properties.climate: Delta swamps + shallow & deepwater blocks, northward gas grid.
properties.landmarks: ["NLNG Bonny Terminal","EGTL Escravos","AKK gas pipeline","Oben / Oben-Geregu","Obiafu-Obrikom"]
properties.highlights: ["Largest gas reserves in Africa","NLNG #1 African LNG exporter","AKK pipeline to northern consumers","Gas flare commercialisation"]

properties.name: Coal (Enugu / Middle Belt)
properties.summary: Historic Enugu sub-bituminous coalfields — Nigeria's first mineral export, now targeting power & cement.
properties.description: Coal was Nigeria's first systematic solid-mineral industry, with the Enugu (Udi hills) fields powering port railways and export trade from Port Harcourt by the 1920s–50s. Modern efforts focus on sub-bituminous coal for captive power, cement blending, and proposed mine-mouth power stations (Kogi, Benue, Enugu, and Nasarawa).

properties.climate: Guinea savanna–forest transition belt, Udi and Mambilla foothills.

properties.name: Tin & Columbite (Jos Plateau)
properties.summary: World-famous Jos Plateau alluvial tin and columbite deposits — a 20th-century mining legacy.
properties.description: Tin and columbite (niobium-tantalum ore) were mined on the Jos Plateau from 1904 through the 1970s, driven by dredging of alluvial gravels. This created the landscape of mine ponds, reclaimed farmlands, and gullies that still shape the plateau. Remnant artisanal workings continue, and Nigeria is now exploring rare-metal pegmatites downstream of old leases.
properties.reserveNote: Pegmatites with tin-tantalum-niobium still in-situ; reserve estimates vary
properties.productionNote: Peak 1960s production made Nigeria a leading tin supplier; artisanal only today
properties.type: Cassiterite tin, columbite (niobium), tantalite & lithium-cesium-tantalum pegmatites
properties.economy: Heritage mining; current artisanal tin + rare metals exploration for batteries market.
properties.climate: Highland Jos Plateau climate; cooler, rainfall influenced by orography.
properties.landmarks: ["Jos Museum of Traditional Nigerian Architecture + mining exhibits","Barikin Ladi mining ponds","Kuru / Rayfield heritage areas"]
properties.highlights: ["Jos alluvial tin heritage","Columbite-tantalum (rare metals)","Mine pond & erosion landscape"]
properties.products: ["Tin metal (Sn) – solders for electronics assembly","Tinplate – food & beverage cans, aerosol containers","Tin alloys – bronze, bearing metals, pewter, fusible alloys","Niobium (columbite) – high-strength low-alloy (HSLA) steel for pipelines & structural","Niobium superalloys – jet engines, gas turbines, rocket nozzles","Tantalum (from columbite-tantalite ores) – electrolytic capacitors for phones & EVs","Lithium byproducts (from Jos pegmatites) – Li-ion battery precursor salts","Tin chemicals – PVC heat stabilisers, plating, catalysts, glass polishing"]

properties.name: Iron Ore (Itakpe, Agbaja & Koton-Karfe)
properties.summary: Itakpe iron-ore deposit supplies the Ajaokuta Steel Complex and the National Iron Ore Mining Company (NIOMCO).
properties.description: Nigeria's principal iron ore deposits are the Itakpe hematite-magnetite ore (Kogi) and the Agbaja oolitic iron formation (Kogi/Enugu). NIOMCO at Itakpe ships beneficiated ore via rail to Ajaokuta and Delta Steel (Aladja), supporting Nigeria's long-delayed domestic steel programme. Recent interest includes direct-reduction iron for the Dangote-led Obajana/Ajaokuta revival efforts.
properties.reserveNote: Itakpe proven + Agbaja indicated >2 billion tonnes of iron-formation
properties.productionNote: NIOMCO: ~1-2 Mtpa beneficiated pellets/ore for Ajaokuta & Aladja
properties.type: Itakpe magnetite-hematite, Agbaja oolitic iron, NSIA-backed Itakpe pellet upgrade
properties.economy: Steel industry feedstock, Ajaokuta & Aladja steel mills supply chain.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna on the Kogi plateau; proximity to Niger confluence.

properties.summary: Emerging artisanal-to-industrial gold province across Zamfara, Kebbi, Kaduna, Osun and Niger.
properties.description: Nigeria is increasingly recognised as a gold-bearing nation. Primary activity is artisanal and small-scale gold mining (ASGM) across a northwest Zamfara–Kebbi–Kaduna belt, plus the Ife-Ilesha schist belt in Osun/Ekiti. Formal large-scale mines are now under development, with the Presidential Artisanal Gold Mining Initiative (PAGMI) seeking to formalise production and reduce security and child-labour risks.

properties.name: Limestone (Cement Belts)
properties.summary: Extensive Maastrichtian limestone formations backing the Obajana, Sokoto, Calabar, and Mfamosing cement plants.
properties.description: Nigeria's cement industry relies on thick Maastrichtian limestone sequences: (1) the Sokoto embayment (Sokoto cement plant), (2) the Nkalagu/Mfamosing belt east of the Niger (Dangote Obajana, Calabar cement, Lafarge Ashaka/Ugwuaji), and (3) smaller Ewekoro/Sagamu deposits north of Lagos. These deposits underpin Africa's largest cement producer (Dangote Cement) and the wider construction sector.
properties.reserveNote: Tens of billions of tonnes — enough for 500+ years at current production
properties.productionNote: Nigeria ~70+ Mtpa cement; Dangote Obajana alone >16 Mtpa
properties.type: Maastrichtian limestone (Nkalagu, Mfamosing, Kalambaina, Ewekoro, Ashaka, Gombe)
properties.economy: Cement manufacturing (Dangote, Lafarge-Holcim, BUA, Cement Co. of Northern Nigeria).
properties.climate: Sudan-savanna in the north, tropical forest–savanna transitions in the southeast.
properties.landmarks: ["Obajana Cement (Kogi, Dangote)","Ashaka Cement (Gombe, Lafarge)","Sokoto Cement","Mfamosing / Calabar Cement","Ewekoro Cement (Ogun)"]
properties.highlights: ["Backbone of Dangote African cement empire","Maastrichtian limestone belts","Obajana #1 Africa cement plant"]
properties.products: ["Portland cement (OPC) – the dominant use (Obajana, Dangote, BUA, Ashaka, etc.)","Ready-mix concrete & precast concrete products","Construction & road aggregate – crushed limestone for base courses & chippings","Agricultural lime / ground calcium carbonate (GCC) – soil pH correction","Sodium carbonate (soda ash) & calcium chloride – detergents, glass, de-icers","Precipitated calcium carbonate (PCC) – paint, paper coating, plastics filler","Flux material – iron & steelmaking blast furnaces and smelting","Glass manufacturing – soda-lime glass for bottles, windows, tableware","Filler in rubber, pharmaceuticals (calcium supplements), toothpaste, cosmetics"]

properties.name: Bitumen & Tar Sands (Dahomey Basin, Ondo)
properties.summary: Onshore heavy-oil / tar-sand belt in Ondo/Edo – one of Africa's largest bitumen reserves.
properties.description: Nigeria's eastern Dahomey basin holds extensive bitumen and tar-sand deposits, predominantly in Ondo and adjacent Edo/Ogun. properties.name: Lead-Zinc (Lower Benue Trough)
properties.summary: Mississippi-Valley style lead-zinc mineralisation across Benue, Taraba, Nasarawa, Plateau belts.
properties.description: Nigeria hosts a well-defined lead-zinc-silver mineral belt in the Albian–Turonian carbonates of the Lower Benue Trough and on the Jos Plateau margins. Deposits at Abakaliki (Ebonyi), Barikin Ladi and environs (Plateau), and in the Ibi-Muri belt (Taraba) have seen decades of artisanal mining, with modern ESG-focused juniors seeking to bring polymetallic (Pb, Zn, Ag, Cd, Cu) production online.
properties.reserveNote: Millions of tonnes indicated Pb-Zn with Ag, Cd byproducts
properties.productionNote: Artisanal Pb-Zn dominant; several formal-scale feasibility projects
properties.type: Carbonate-hosted MVT Pb-Zn + vein Ag-Cd polymetallic ores
properties.economy: Zinc galvanising, lead acid batteries, silver credits, growing junior mining.
properties.climate: Benue trough Guinea savanna; Jos Plateau highlands.
properties.landmarks: ["Abakaliki Pb-Zn field (Ebonyi)","Ibi-Muri belt (Taraba)","Barkin Ladi Pb-Zn veins (Plateau)"]
properties.highlights: ["Abakaliki MVT field","Polymetallic byproducts (Ag/Cd)","Benue-Trough belt"]
properties.products: ["Lead-acid batteries – automotive SLI, motive power (forklifts), stationary UPS backup","Galvanised steel – zinc coating on rebars, roofing sheets, pipes (corrosion protection)","Brass & bronze alloys – plumbing valves, fittings, bearings, decorative hardware","Zinc die-castings – automotive components, door handles, electrical housings","Silver bullion byproduct – from lead-silver smelting (Pb-Ag ores)","Cadmium plating & battery byproducts – historically, now restricted but still relevant","Zinc oxide (ZnO) – tyres (vulcanising activator), pharmaceuticals, sunscreen, ceramics","Zinc chemicals – dry-cell batteries, fertilisers (Zn micronutrient), pigments"]

properties.summary: Lake Chad solar salt pans, inland brines in Nasarawa/Benue, and Lagos lagoon-evaporation salt.
properties.description: Salt production in Nigeria comes from three sources: (1) solar evaporation in the Lake Chad–Komadougu Yobe basin, (2) inland salt springs and brine pans in Nasarawa (Keana), Benue, and Plateau, and (3) coastal lagoon-evaporation schemes around Lagos/Ogun. properties.name: Bauxite & Alumina (Mambilla / Adamawa Plateau Belt)
properties.summary: Lateritic bauxite plateaus in Taraba, Adamawa, and Ekiti — feedstock for Nigerian aluminium smelters and export.
properties.description: Nigeria's bauxite occurs as duricrust lateritic caps on the Mambilla Plateau, the Adamawa highlands, the Jos Plateau outliers, and smaller deposits in Ekiti. Current small-scale production feeds the local aluminium extrusion industry, while NSIA-backed feasibility studies target a 1–2 Mtpa bauxite mine + integrated alumina refinery paired with Mambilla hydropower.
properties.reserveNote: ~900 Mt lateritic bauxite indicated; Mambilla alone ~350 Mt
properties.productionNote: Artisanal + small crushing; NSIA Mambilla bauxite–alumina projects in pre-FEED
properties.type: Gibbsite-boehmite lateritic bauxite on plateau surfaces; export-grade alumina potential
properties.economy: Aluminium metal feedstock, alumina refining, construction extrusion, and export concentrate.
properties.climate: Highland tropical; bauxite laterites require seasonal wet–dry leaching.
properties.landmarks: ["Mambilla Plateau bauxite laterites (Taraba)","Adamawa (Numan/Shelleng) bauxite caps","Aluminium extrusion smelters (Ikeja, Port Harcourt)"]
properties.highlights: ["Mambilla Plateau bauxite belt","NSIA alumina refinery (planned)","Domestic aluminium extrusion supply"]

properties.name: Gemstones (Sapphire, Ruby, Aquamarine, Tourmaline — Plateau & Kaduna)
properties.summary: High-value coloured gemstone fields in Plateau, Kaduna, and Nasarawa — sapphire, ruby, aquamarine, tourmaline.
properties.description: Nigeria is an emerging coloured-gemstone producer. The Jos Plateau and neighbouring Kaduna/Nasarawa pegmatites and schists produce aquamarine, emerald, tourmaline, topaz, garnet, zircon, and pink/blue sapphire, with ruby deposits in the Mambilla (Taraba). Gemstone cutting is informal in Kaduna's lapidaries, but the Federal Ministry of Mines & Steel Development operates a gemstone certification lab to formalise the value chain.
properties.reserveNote: Gemstone-grade deposits widespread; not conventionally quantified as reserves
properties.productionNote: Artisanal small-scale mining + Kaduna lapidaries; formal certification growing
properties.type: Beryl (aquamarine/emerald), corundum (sapphire/ruby), tourmaline, topaz, garnet, zircon
properties.economy: Gemstone cutting, jewellery manufacturing, export of rough & cut stones, certification lab.
properties.climate: Highland tropical (Jos Plateau) to Sudan savanna; pegmatite and alluvial fields.
properties.landmarks: ["Plateau Shendam / Bokkos aquamarine fields","Kaduna gemstone lapidary district","Federal Mines Gemstone Certification Laboratory (Abuja/Kaduna)","Taraba Mambilla ruby occurrences"]
properties.highlights: ["Sapphire, ruby & aquamarine fields","Jos Plateau pegmatite gem belt","Kaduna lapidary & cutting hub"]
properties.products: ["Faceted cut gemstones (sapphire, ruby, emerald, aquamarine, tourmaline, topaz)","Fine jewellery – rings, necklaces, earrings, bracelets, wedding sets (gold + gems)","Cabochons – opaque/translucent stones (star sapphire, garnet, jasper) set in jewellery","Gemstone beads – Nigerian traditional coral & gem beadwork for regalia","Industrial / collector specimens – mineral crystal collections & museum-grade pieces","Semi-precious inlay & mosaic tiles – decorative architectural stone cladding","Certified rough exports – IGI/MGS-graded rough stones for overseas cutters","Watch dials & luxury accessories – hardstone inlays for premium timepieces"]

properties.name: Kaolin & Ball Clays (Ajaokuta, Warri, Abakaliki, Bauchi)
properties.summary: Sedimentary kaolin and refractory ball-clay deposits for ceramics, paper coating, and drilling muds.
properties.description: Nigeria's kaolin deposits occur in Cretaceous/Tertiary sedimentary basins: Ajaokuta–Okene (Kogi), Warri southern flank (Delta), Abakaliki (Ebonyi), and the Bauchi/Gombe formation clays. Ball clays also outcrop in the Ilesha schist belt (Osun/Ekiti). Uses span ceramics tableware, paper coating, and oil-drilling mud additives, with Dangote & Bua cement plants also consuming raw clays.

properties.name: Phosphate Rock (Sokoto Embayment & Cross River Basin)
properties.summary: Sokoto marine phosphorites and Cross River phosphate shales — fertiliser and animal-feed mineral.
properties.description: Nigeria's phosphate deposits occur principally in the Upper Cretaceous Maastrichtian Sokoto embayment (Gwandu, Illela, and Isa formations) and in phosphorite nodules and shales along the Cross River basin (Odukpani, Ikom). Current output feeds local single-superphosphate (SSP) blending, with a Morocco-backed Sokoto greenfield fertiliser complex under negotiation.
properties.reserveNote: Sokoto embayment indicated ~250 Mt phosphate rock equivalent; Cross River ~50 Mt
properties.productionNote: Small artisanal + SSP blending; Sokoto Morocco-JV DAP/NPK fertiliser plant planned
properties.type: Marine sedimentary phosphorites, shale-hosted phosphate nodules; DAP/NPK fertiliser grades
properties.economy: Fertiliser (SSP, DAP, NPK blends), animal-feed dicalcium phosphate, industrial acid.
properties.climate: Sahelian Sokoto plains + tropical Cross River; both marine transgression sequences.
properties.landmarks: ["Sokoto Gwandu / Illela phosphorite deposits","Cross River Odukpani/Ikom phosphate nodules","National Fertiliser Company of Nigeria (NAFCON) blending terminals"]
properties.highlights: ["Sokoto marine phosphorite belt","NAFCON fertiliser feedstock","Morocco JV Sokoto DAP plant (MOU)"]
properties.products: ["Single Superphosphate (SSP) fertiliser – P₂O₅ + gypsum soil amendment","Di-ammonium Phosphate (DAP) & Mono-ammonium Phosphate (MAP) – granular NPK fertilisers","NPK compound blends (15-15-15, 20-10-10) – cocoa, maize, rice, oil palm nutrition","Phosphoric acid (wet process) – H₃PO₄ for DAP + food-grade derivatives","Dicalcium phosphate (DCP) & Monocalcium phosphate (MCP) – poultry & livestock feed minerals","Triple Superphosphate (TSP) – high-concentration P₂O₅ direct-application fertiliser","Industrial phosphate chemicals – STPP detergents, food emulsifiers, flame retardants","Superphosphate of lime (SSP) byproduct gypsum – plasterboard & cement retarder"]

properties.name: Phosphate Rock (Sokoto Embayment & Cross River Basin)
properties.summary: Sokoto marine phosphorites and Cross River phosphate shales — fertiliser and animal-feed mineral.
properties.description: Nigeria's phosphate deposits occur principally in the Upper Cretaceous Maastrichtian Sokoto embayment (Gwandu, Illela, and Isa formations) and in phosphorite nodules and shales along the Cross River basin (Odukpani, Ikom). properties.name: Gypsum & Anhydrite (Sokoto, Niger, Benue, Gombe)
properties.summary: Evaporitic gypsum deposits supplying cement retarder, plasterboard, and agricultural soil conditioner.
properties.description: Nigeria's gypsum deposits are predominantly evaporitic in the Sokoto embayment, the Benue trough, southern Niger State, and the Gombe sub-basin. The overwhelming bulk of output feeds the cement industry (5% gypsum added to clinker as set retarder), with the remainder used in wallboard, plaster, agriculture, and dental plasters.

properties.economy: Cement retarder (largest demand), plasterboard, agricultural gypsum (soil amendment).
properties.climate: Sahelian–Sudan evaporitic lake basins with Cretaceous–Tertiary marine sequences.
properties.landmarks: ["Sokoto–Argungu gypsum deposits","Benue Makurdi/Lafia gypsum sub-basins","Dangote/Lafarge cement blending & clinker grinding lines"]

properties.name: Graphite (Nasarawa, Ondo, Ekiti Schist Belts)
properties.summary: Flake & vein graphite in the Nigerian schist belts — emerging lithium-ion battery anode material.
properties.description: Nigeria contains graphite-bearing metasediments within the Proterozoic schist belts running through Nasarawa, Ondo, Ekiti, and Kwara. Flake graphite concentrates command premium prices for refractories and expandable graphite, while the electric-vehicle era has drawn attention to high-purity spheroidised graphite for Li-ion anodes. Junior explorers active since 2021 have delineated maiden resource estimates.
properties.reserveNote: Indicated maiden resources >50 Mt at multiple projects; upgradeable to battery-grade
properties.productionNote: Early-stage; artisanal flake + junior pre-production; graphite spheroidisation plants studied
properties.type: Flake graphite (+ vein graphite) in schist metasediments; expandable + battery grades
properties.economy: Refractories, steel recarburising, Li-ion battery anodes, graphene feedstock.
properties.climate: Tropical highland; schist-belt basement terrains with weathered outcrops.
properties.landmarks: ["Nasarawa graphite schist belts (Akwanga, Lafia)","Ondo/Ekiti Ife–Ilesha schist graphite occurrences","Nigerian Coal Corporation (NCC) graphite diversification research"]
properties.highlights: ["Schist-belt flake graphite","Li-ion battery anode (future)","Expandable graphite & refractories"]
properties.products: ["Natural flake graphite (80–98% C) – refractory crucibles, brake linings, foundry facings","Battery-grade spheroidised & coated graphite – Li-ion battery anodes (EVs, grid storage)","Expandable graphite (EG) – intumescent fire-retardant, thermal interface sheets, gaskets","Graphite electrodes (artificial from needle coke) – electric arc furnace steelmaking","Steelmaking recarburiser – low-sulphur graphite for carbon addition to ladles","Pencil leads & lubricants – bonded clay/graphite for writing & industrial lubrication","Graphene precursor – high-purity graphite feed for CVD & liquid exfoliation","Nuclear graphite (speciality) – pebbles & moderator blocks for next-gen HTGRs"]

properties.name: Feldspar, Mica & Industrial Minerals (Nasarawa-Kwara, Ogun-Ekiti)
properties.summary: Industrial silica, feldspar, kaolin & mica assemblage powering Nigerian ceramics, glass, and paint industries.
properties.description: A full ceramic-grade industrial-mineral assemblage crops out in the Nigerian basement: potash feldspar in Nasarawa and Kwara, soda feldspar in the Ogun-Ekiti crystalline basement, muscovite mica in the Ibadan schists, and silica sands in the Niger-Benue delta fringes. Together with the abundant kaolin clays, they underpin Nigeria's rapidly growing domestic tile, sanitaryware, float-glass, and bottle-glass industries.
properties.reserveNote: Vast pegmatite feldspar + alluvial silica sands; mica widespread
properties.productionNote: Small-scale pegmatite mining + river silica; ceramic-grade beneficiation growing
properties.type: K-feldspar (microcline), Na-feldspar (albite), muscovite mica, silica sand; ceramic/glass grades
properties.economy: Ceramic tile flux, glass batch, filler extenders, cosmetics, electrical insulation.
properties.climate: Basement-craton tropical highlands + deltaic alluvial silica terrains.
properties.landmarks: ["Nasarawa Lafia/Akwanga pegmatite feldspar belts","Ogun–Ewekoro silica sands (west of Abeokuta)","Niger–Benue delta fringe silica-sand dredges (Warri, Onitsha)"]
properties.highlights: ["Ceramic-grade feldspar + silica","Pegmatite K-feldspar belt Nasarawa","Mica for electrical & cosmetic grades"]
properties.products: ["Ceramic tile flux (K-feldspar) – vitrified & porcelain floor/wall tiles vitrification","Glass batch feldspar + silica sand – soda-lime float-glass (windows, mirrors) & bottles","Dinnerware sanitaryware vitreous china batch – feldspar + kaolin + silica + ball clay","Muscovite mica sheet – high-voltage electrical insulation, capacitor dielectrics, furnace windows","Mica powder (wet- & dry-ground) – paint extender, pearlescent pigment substrate, cosmetics","Silica-sand foundry moulds (AFS 45–55 grade) – green-sand iron & steel casting","Filler extenders – ground silica & feldspar powder for paints, plastics, rubber, adhesives","Speciality low-iron silica (SiO₂ >99.5%) – solar PV glass, ultra-clear optical glass, fibre optics"]

properties.name: Feldspar, Mica & Industrial Minerals (Nasarawa-Kwara, Ogun-Ekiti)
properties.summary: Industrial silica, feldspar, kaolin & mica assemblage powering Nigerian ceramics, glass, and paint industries.
properties.description: A full ceramic-grade industrial-mineral assemblage crops out in the Nigerian basement: potash feldspar in Nasarawa and Kwara, soda feldspar in the Ogun-Ekiti crystalline basement, muscovite mica in the Ibadan schists, and silica sands in the Niger-Benue delta fringes. properties.name: Barite / Baryte (Benue Trough)
properties.summary: Africa's largest known barite deposits, centred on Azara (Nasarawa) and the Benue Trough — the key domestic drilling-mud feedstock.
properties.description: Barite (barium sulfate) occurs as vein and residual deposits along the Benue Trough, most notably the large Azara deposit in Nasarawa State plus occurrences around Katsina-Ala (Benue), Wukari (Taraba), and parts of Cross River. Nigeria's oil and gas sector has historically imported most of its drilling-mud barite despite these reserves, making Azara a flagship import-substitution project for the upstream sector.
properties.reserveNote: Hundreds of millions of tonnes indicated; Azara ranked among Africa's largest barite deposits
properties.productionNote: Small-to-medium scale mining supplying domestic drilling-mud demand; import substitution drive ongoing
properties.type: Barite (barium sulfate) vein and residual/eluvial deposits
properties.economy: Oilfield drilling-mud weighting agent import substitution; paint, rubber, and radiation-shielding fillers.
properties.climate: Guinea savanna, Benue Trough basement-sediment terrain.
properties.landmarks: ["Azara Barite Mine (Nasarawa)","Katsina-Ala barite belt","Cross River barite occurrences"]
properties.highlights: ["Africa's largest known barite reserves","Oil & gas drilling-mud import substitution","Benue Trough mineral belt"]

properties.name: Diatomite (Borno / Lake Chad Basin)
properties.summary: Diatomaceous-earth deposits in the Lake Chad basin, valued for filtration, insulation, and absorbent applications.

properties.name: Rutile, Ilmenite & Zircon (Coastal Heavy Mineral Sands)
properties.summary: Titanium-zirconium-bearing beach and alluvial placer sands along the Atlantic coast, a prospective titanium-pigment feedstock.
properties.description: Heavy mineral sand placers containing rutile, ilmenite, and zircon occur along stretches of Nigeria's Atlantic coastline, notably in Ogun, Lagos, and Akwa Ibom, as well as alluvial occurrences further inland. These titanium- and zirconium-bearing sands are of growing interest for titanium-dioxide pigment production and zircon refractories, though large-scale mining has yet to be established.

properties.name: Dolomite (Kogi-Cross River Belts)
properties.summary: Calcium-magnesium carbonate dolomite deposits supplying refractory, agricultural-lime, and glass industries.
properties.description: Dolomite deposits are found alongside limestone formations in Kogi State and the Cross River (Mfamosing/Calabar) belt, as well as smaller occurrences in Sokoto. The mineral is processed into refractory bricks for steel-furnace linings, agricultural lime, and magnesium-chemical feedstock, complementing Nigeria's broader limestone-cement belt.

properties.name: Granite & Dimension Stone (Ogun-Nasarawa-Ekiti Quarry Belts)
properties.summary: Widespread basement-complex granite and gneiss quarry belts supplying aggregate and dimension stone for Nigeria's construction industry.
properties.description: Granite and gneiss outcrops of the Precambrian basement complex are quarried extensively around Ogun (Abeokuta's rock outcrops), Nasarawa, Kwara, Ekiti, and Delta states for crushed aggregate and decorative dimension stone. These quarry belts underpin the bulk of Nigeria's road, rail, and building-construction aggregate supply.

properties.productionNote: Widespread active quarrying for crushed aggregate and dimension stone
properties.type: Granite and gneiss basement rock; crushed aggregate and dimension stone grades
properties.economy: Construction aggregate, road/rail ballast, and decorative dimension stone.
properties.climate: Basement-complex terrain spanning rainforest to Guinea savanna.

properties.products: ["Crushed granite aggregate for concrete and road base","Dimension/decorative stone for building facades and monuments","Railway ballast","Kerbstones and paving setts"]

properties.name: Fluorspar (Taraba Belt)
properties.summary: Fluorspar (calcium fluoride) vein occurrences in the Taraba basement belt, prospective flux feedstock for steel and aluminium industries.
properties.description: Fluorspar veins occur within the basement complex of Taraba State around the Wukari-Kentu axis, offering a potential domestic source of the fluxing agent used in steelmaking and aluminium smelting. Development remains at an early exploration stage, with artisanal collection the main current activity.
